req.title: Update unknown returns 404
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when PUT targets a non-existent task id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-011 requires that PUT /tasks/{task_id} returns HTTP 404 when the task_id does not exist. To achieve high mutation kill rate we need: (1) a positive test confirming a known-existing task CAN be updated (200 OK), to distinguish 404-always mutations; (2) a negative test confirming a clearly non-existent id returns exactly 404 with the correct detail body; (3) a boundary test at id=21 (one past the last seeded row, id=20) to catch off-by-one mutations; (4) an additional negative test at id=0 (below the minimum valid id) to cover the lower boundary; (5) a decision-table test verifying the detail message contains the exact task_id, catching constant-substitution mutations. All tests use an in-process SQLite database seeded fresh per test via Base.metadata.create_all + fixture rows.

tests.name: test_put_existing_task_returns_200
preconditions: Database contains task with id=1 (title='Read chapter 5', completed=true)
expected: Response body contains id=1 and updated title
trace: R-TASK-011: positive path — existing task must NOT return 404; catches mutations that always return 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
from app.database import engine, get_db
from app import models
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

with Session(engine) as _s:
    _s.add(models.Task(id=1, title='Read chapter 5', description='Some desc', completed=True))
    _s.commit()

client = TestClient(app)
r = client.put('/tasks/1', json={'title': 'Updated title', 'completed': False})
assert r.status_code == 200
body = r.json()
assert body['id'] == 1
assert body['title'] == 'Updated title'
assert body['completed'] == False
